product_overview: Appcrons is a backend service that keeps free-tier Render.com backend instances alive by sending scheduled HTTP pings and recording ping metrics. This PRD covers the HTTP APIs for authentication, app management, request scheduling/RTFs, admin operations, feedback/bug reports, and monitoring endpoints.

test_generation_rules.MANDATORY_AUTH_FIXTURE: EVERY test that requires authentication MUST first create a fresh user by calling POST /api/v1/auth/signup with a unique UUID-based email (e.g. f'{uuid.uuid4()}@test.com') and password 'TestPass@1234'. The signup response JSON has this shape: {accessToken:'...', status:'success', user:{id:'...', name:'...', email:'...'}}. Extract the 'accessToken' field from the TOP LEVEL of the response (NOT from data.token). Use it as 'Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>' for all subsequent requests. NEVER HARDCODE A JWT TOKEN STRING.
test_generation_rules.MANDATORY_APP_FIXTURE: When a test needs an app, create it via POST /api/v1/apps/post with body {name: f'App {uuid.uuid4()}', url: f'https://app-{uuid.uuid4()}.onrender.com/active', requestInterval: '10'}. The 'name' and 'url' MUST contain uuid4() to be globally unique. 'requestInterval' MUST be a STRING, one of '5', '10', '15'. NEVER use an integer.
test_generation_rules.MANDATORY_TIME_FORMAT: The 'start' and 'end' fields for request time frames MUST be HH:MM:SS strings like '06:00:00' and '23:00:00'. The Go backend expects this exact format with seconds included. NEVER generate HH:MM without seconds. NEVER generate full ISO timestamps or datetime strings. The correct literal values are EXACTLY '06:00:00' and '23:00:00'.
test_generation_rules.MANDATORY_FIELD_NAMES: The app model uses 'isDisabled' (boolean). NEVER use 'isEnabled'. Newly created apps have isDisabled=true by default. The request time model uses fields 'start', 'end', 'timeZone'. NEVER use 'startTime', 'endTime', or 'timezone'.
test_generation_rules.MANDATORY_DISABLE_BEHAVIOR: Disabling an already disabled app returns 400 with message 'app is already disabled'. It is NOT idempotent. To test disable, you MUST first enable the app, then disable it.
test_generation_rules.MANDATORY_CODE_QUALITY: All generated Python test code MUST be syntactically valid. NEVER insert placeholder comments like 'full code' or 'rest of code here' at line 1. NEVER leave incomplete code. Every file must be a complete, runnable Python script.

core_goals: Provide secure JWT-based user and admin authentication and user profile management.
Allow users to register applications to be pinged at configurable intervals and define daily Request Time Frames (RTFs).
Record and expose ping logs and live ping events; ensure scheduler respects RTFs and uses Redis locks for multi-instance safety.
Expose admin endpoints for system-wide stats and user/app inspection (sys_admin only).
Accept and manage user feedback and unauthenticated bug reports; provide health and Prometheus metrics endpoints.

features.name: Authentication API
features.description: Register and authenticate users. The signup response JSON shape is: {accessToken:'<jwt>', status:'success', message:'Signup successfully', user:{id:'<uuid>', name:'<name>', email:'<email>', role:'user'}}. IMPORTANT: The JWT token is at the TOP LEVEL key 'accessToken', NOT nested inside 'data'. Use unique UUID-based emails for every signup to avoid duplicates.
user_flows: POST /api/v1/auth/signup with body {"name":"Test User","email":"<uuid4>@test.com","password":"TestPass@1234"} -> Receive 201 with {accessToken:"<jwt>", status:"success", user:{id:"<uuid>", name:"Test User", email:"..."}}
POST /api/v1/auth/signin with body {"email":"<same-email>","password":"TestPass@1234"} -> Receive 200 with {accessToken:"<jwt>", status:"success", user:{...}}
POST /api/v1/auth/signup with body missing "email" -> Receive 400 with {status:"error", message:"validation error"}
POST /api/v1/auth/signin with wrong password -> Receive 401 with {status:"error", message:"invalid credentials"}
GET /api/v1/auth/user/get/<userId> with no Authorization header -> Receive 401

features.name: App Management API
features.description: SETUP FOR EVERY TEST: Step 1) POST /api/v1/auth/signup with {name:'Test User', email:f'{uuid.uuid4()}@test.com', password:'TestPass@1234'} -> extract 'accessToken' from TOP LEVEL of response JSON. Step 2) Use 'Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>' for all subsequent calls. Step 3) When creating an app, use {name:f'App {uuid.uuid4()}', url:f'https://app-{uuid.uuid4()}.onrender.com/active', requestInterval:'10'}. FIELD RULES: 'requestInterval' is ALWAYS a STRING ('5','10','15'). The field 'isDisabled' (NOT 'isEnabled') indicates if app is disabled. New apps have isDisabled=true by default. DISABLE IS NOT IDEMPOTENT: calling disable on an already disabled app returns 400 with message 'app is already disabled'. To test disable, first ENABLE the app, THEN disable it.
user_flows: FIXTURE: POST /api/v1/auth/signup with {name:'Test User', email:f'{uuid.uuid4()}@test.com', password:'TestPass@1234'} -> 201 -> extract response.json()['accessToken'] as TOKEN. Then POST /api/v1/apps/post with Authorization: Bearer TOKEN and body {name:f'App {uuid.uuid4()}', url:f'https://app-{uuid.uuid4()}.onrender.com/active', requestInterval:'10'} -> Receive 201 with {status:'success', data:{app:{id:'<appId>', isDisabled:true, requestInterval:'10', ...}}}

PATCH /api/v1/apps/update/<appId> with Authorization: Bearer TOKEN and body {name:f'Updated {uuid.uuid4()}', url:f'https://upd-{uuid.uuid4()}.onrender.com/active', requestInterval:'15'} -> Receive 200 with updated app

PATCH /api/v1/apps/enable/<appId> with Authorization: Bearer TOKEN -> Receive 200 with {status:'success', data:{app:{isDisabled:false}}}. WARNING: Enable is NOT idempotent. Calling enable on an already enabled app returns 400 'app is already enabled'. Since new apps start with isDisabled=true, simply call enable ONCE on the freshly created app. Do NOT call enable twice.

To test DISABLE: First ENABLE the app (PATCH /enable/<appId>) since new apps start disabled, then PATCH /api/v1/apps/disable/<appId> with Authorization: Bearer TOKEN -> Receive 200 with {status:'success', data:{app:{isDisabled:true}}}. WARNING: Calling disable on an already disabled app returns 400 'app is already disabled'. Do NOT call disable twice.

DELETE /api/v1/apps/delete/<appId> with Authorization: Bearer TOKEN -> Receive 200. IMPORTANT: Only delete apps that were created by the same user who is authenticated. Do NOT attempt to delete apps with a different user's token (that returns 403 permission error). Do NOT test deleting non-existent apps with random UUIDs.

features.name: Requests API (Request Time Frames & Ping Logs)
features.description: SETUP FOR EVERY TEST: Step 1) POST /api/v1/auth/signup with {name:'Test User', email:f'{uuid.uuid4()}@test.com', password:'TestPass@1234'} -> extract 'accessToken' from TOP LEVEL of response. Step 2) Create an app: POST /api/v1/apps/post with Authorization: Bearer <accessToken> and {name:f'App {uuid.uuid4()}', url:f'https://app-{uuid.uuid4()}.onrender.com/active', requestInterval:'10'} -> extract app id from response.json()['data']['app']['id']. Step 3) Use the extracted token and appId for all request time calls. FIELD NAMES: Use 'start', 'end', 'timeZone' exactly. NEVER use 'startTime', 'endTime', or 'timezone'. TIME FORMAT: 'start' and 'end' MUST be HH:MM:SS strings WITH SECONDS, exactly like '06:00:00' or '23:00:00'. The Go backend REQUIRES seconds. ABSOLUTELY NEVER generate '06:00' (missing seconds), full datetime strings like '2026-04-14 06:00.000000 +0300 EAT', or any ISO timestamp.
user_flows: FIXTURE: signup -> extract accessToken -> create app -> extract appId. Then POST /api/v1/requests/post-request-time with Authorization: Bearer <accessToken> and body {appId:'<extracted-appId>', start:'06:00:00', end:'23:00:00', timeZone:'Africa/Kampala'} -> Receive 201 with {status:'success', data:{requestTime:{...}}}

GET /api/v1/requests/get-live with Authorization: Bearer <accessToken> -> Receive 200 SSE stream. Test should open connection, wait max 5 seconds for any data or heartbeat, and pass if connection was established with 200 status. Do NOT assert on specific event content.

features.name: Admin API
features.description: System administration endpoints for sys_admin users to list users, inspect their apps and requests, and retrieve system statistics. All admin endpoints require a sys_admin JWT (see PRD page 11).
user_flows: POST /api/v1/auth/signin-admin with body {"email":"admin@example.com","password":"AdminPass"} -> Receive 200 with {status:"success", data:{user:{...}, token:"<admin-jwt>"}} -> GET /api/v1/admin/users with Authorization: Bearer <admin-jwt> -> Receive 200 with list of users
GET /api/v1/admin/users/6ba7b810-9dad-11d1-80b4-00c04fd430c8/apps with Authorization: Bearer <admin-jwt> -> Receive 200 with that user's apps
GET /api/v1/admin/users/6ba7b810-9dad-11d1-80b4-00c04fd430c8/apps/3d6f4890-7b21-41d5-b2d3-4f9e8c6a1b2d/requests with Authorization: Bearer <admin-jwt> -> Receive 200 with app request logs
GET /api/v1/admin/stats with Authorization: Bearer <regular-user-token> (not sys_admin) -> Receive 403 with {status:"error", message:"forbidden"}
GET /api/v1/admin/users with no Authorization header -> Receive 401 with {status:"error", message:"missing or invalid token"}

features.name: Feedback API
features.description: SETUP: POST /api/v1/auth/signup with {name:'Test User', email:f'{uuid.uuid4()}@test.com', password:'TestPass@1234'} -> extract 'accessToken' from TOP LEVEL of response. Use as Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>. The feedback post body requires keys 'email' (use the same email from signup) and 'message'.
user_flows: FIXTURE: signup -> extract accessToken. Then POST /api/v1/feedback/post with Authorization: Bearer <accessToken> and body {message:'Love the service', rating:5} -> Receive 201 with created feedback entry
POST /api/v1/feedback/post with no Authorization header -> Receive 401

features.name: Bug Report API
features.description: Endpoints for submitting bug reports. Bug reporting endpoints are unauthenticated by design so users can report issues without logging in (see codebase endpoints).
user_flows: POST /api/v1/bugreport/post with body {"title":"Ping failing","description":"Pings return 503"} and no Authorization header -> Receive 201 with created bug report (status:"success")
GET /api/v1/bugreport/get-all -> Receive 200 with array of bug reports

GET /api/v1/bugreport/get-by-user (unauthenticated) with query param userId=6ba7b810-9dad-11d1-80b4-00c04fd430c8 -> Receive 200 with array of reports for that user (if implemented) or 400 if malformed userId -> Receive 400 with {status:"error", message:"malformed uuid"}
POST /api/v1/bugreport/post with malformed body (missing required fields) -> Receive 400 with {status:"error", message:"validation error"}

features.name: Miscellaneous / Monitoring API
features.description: Simple unauthenticated endpoints for health checks and Prometheus metrics used by monitoring and uptime checks (see PRD page 14).
user_flows: GET /get/active -> Receive 200 with small keep-alive payload (used by external pingers to keep service alive)
GET /metrics -> Receive 200 with Prometheus metrics plaintext body
GET /metrics with heavy load -> Receive 200 (metrics should be served even under higher load); any server error -> Receive 500 with {status:"error", message:"internal server error"}
